language_task: Seperate the food and the toys into the two bowls.
outcome_evidence: Sorting remains incomplete in this observed window. overhead_cam shows the orange fruit-shaped item outside both bowls at frames 1400, 1514, 1644 and 1749, without any transfer. wrist_cam shows repeated finger closing and reopening near that item rather than acquisition and transport. Completion is unconfirmed, while sustained unproductive behavior is visible; no completed lift followed by dropping is established. This outcome is provisional because earlier execution beyond the two context frames and later execution are unavailable.

failure_annotations.explanation: overhead_cam shows the arm remaining at essentially the same tabletop location throughout frames 1400–1749. wrist_cam shows repeated closing/reopening cycles, including frames 1407–1433, 1489–1514, 1617–1644 and 1728–1749, with the orange item remaining outside the bowls and no meaningful sorting progress. This is sustained unproductive behavior, not merely a brief pause; finger motion and occlusion do not establish possession or a hardware fault. Context frames 1398–1399 show the same positioning, supporting continuity at the starting boundary, but the earlier onset is unseen. The behavior may continue beyond frame 1749; the window boundary does not establish termination.
failure_annotations.recovery: Stop repeating the same finger motion, reassess the item's position, and reposition the gripper to obtain a secure grasp; visually confirm acquisition before transporting it to the appropriate food bowl. No visible condition requires human intervention.
failure_annotations.severity_evidence: The visible consequence is delayed, incomplete sorting; neither overhead_cam nor wrist_cam establishes damage, spilling, or a meaningful damage risk.
failure_annotations.resetability_evidence: The item remains accessible on the tabletop and both bowls remain upright, so another attempt needs no environmental reset or human intervention.
